Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Company Launches Women-Centric ‘Nari Suraksha’ Life Insurance Plan
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has introduced a new women-focused insurance product, Nepal Life Nari Suraksha Jeevan Beema Yojana, on the occasion of International Women’s Day, claiming it as the first policy in Nepal designed exclusively with features tailored to women’s needs.
The plan is aimed at providing comprehensive protection covering life security, health, savings, and long-term financial stability. Key features include annual cash benefits based on the insured amount and a progressive death benefit that increases by 25 percent every five years.
Notably, the policy introduces maternity-related benefits in Nepal’s life insurance sector. It offers financial support for pregnancy care and covers 11 serious pregnancy-related complications, providing a lump-sum payment of Rs 100,000 in such cases, along with an additional Rs 10,000 for maternity healthcare expenses. The scheme is available to women aged 18 to 65, with a minimum sum assured of Rs 250,000 and optional riders such as accident death benefit, total permanent disability coverage, and premium waiver facility.
The company said the plan is designed to enhance women’s financial independence, dignity, and future security through accessible and inclusive insurance coverage.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Launches ‘Super Term Life Insurance’ in Partnership With eSewa
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited, in collaboration with digital payment service provider eSewa, has launched a new term life insurance plan titled ‘Super Term Life Insurance’. The one-year policy aims to reduce financial risk for families in unforeseen situations by offering high life insurance coverage at affordable premiums.
Starting from an annual premium of Rs. 725, insured individuals can receive coverage ranging from Rs. 5 lakh to Rs. 20 lakh. Available to citizens aged 18 to 60, the policy covers both accidental and natural death and can be easily purchased through the eSewa app, reflecting the company’s commitment to accessible and customer-friendly insurance solutions.

Headline: Nepal Life Hosts MDRT Achievers Award 2026 Honoring Top Insurance Agents
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company successfully organized the MDRT Achievers Award 2026 from Magh 13–15, 2082 BS at Pokhara Grande, honoring 110 qualified agents for their performance from January to December 2025.
The three-day event was inaugurated by CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli and featured key speeches from company directors, sales heads, and insurance federation representatives, emphasizing agent development, professionalism, and promoting life insurance awareness in Nepal.
Parajuli highlighted the role of agents as the backbone of the company and encouraged expanding insurance reach nationwide. The program also included musical performances, comedy acts, and motivational sessions to celebrate and inspire the achievers.

Headline: Nepal Life Recognized as Top Life Insurance Company at HRM Awards
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has been honored with “The HRM Awards for Corporate Excellence 2025” in the Life Insurance category by Corporate Club Nepal.
The award recognizes Nepal Life’s outstanding performance based on financial health, governance, claims settlement ratio, capital, premium collection, HR development, investment diversification, digital transformation, and corporate social responsibility initiatives.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli and Deputy CEO Amit Kumar Keyal received the award at a grand ceremony in Kathmandu. Parajuli expressed gratitude to the board, employees, agents, regulators, shareholders, and customers, emphasizing that collective efforts will continue to promote the importance and utility of life insurance in Nepal.

Headline: Life and Non-Life Insurance Sectors Report Varied Performance in Premium Collection Till Poush FY 2082/83
Full Content:
Insurance companies are competing with each other to increase their premium collection. Till the 6 months of the fiscal year 2082/83, i.e., Poush end, the life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 94.38 Arba, out of their 11,455,235 total active insurance policies.
As per the report published by Nepal Insurance Authority, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited limited single-handedly collected Rs. 25.51 Arba, having an active number of insurance policies of 1,745,933 as of Poush 2082.
Meanwhile, the most striking revelation comes from Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Co Ltd, which boasts the highest number of active insurance policies 2,431,856. However, the company generated only Rs. 2.94 Arba in premiums during the assessed period.
Coming towards the non-life insurance sector, Shikhar Insurance Company collected the highest premium worth Rs. 2.77 arba. Likewise, Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Limited, which has 133,022 insurance policies, collected a premium worth Rs. 2.61 arba as its insurance premium.
The non-life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 23.67 Arba out of its 1,420,548 total active insurance policies.

Headline: Public Issue "Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana" Mutual Fund Scheme Closing Today
Full Content:
Nepal Life Capital Limited is closing the issue of its mutual fund scheme
"Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana"
to the general public today, 4th Magh, 2082. The issue opened on the 9th Magh, 2082.
Out of 16 crore unit shares, 14%, i.e., 2.24 crores units worth Rs. 22,40,00,000, have been allocated to the scheme manager, Nepal Life Insurance Limited, and 1%, i.e., 16,00,000 units worth Rs. 1.60 crores, have been allocated to the fund sponsor, Nepal Life Capital Limited. The remaining 13,60,00,000 units worth Rs 1.36 Arba will be issued to the general public and institutions.
According to CDSC, 77,711 applicants have applied for 18,73,58,800 units worth Rs. 1.87 Arba so far.
"Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana" is a closed-ended fund. Applicants can apply for a minimum of 100 units to a maximum of 1,60,00,000 units.
This is the first mutual fund scheme that Nepal Life Capital Limited will manage.
There are currently 41 closed-end mutual funds listed on the Nepal Stock Exchange, whereas 12 open-end schemes are traded directly with the respective fund manager.

Headline: Nepal Life Launches “Samriddhi Lagani Yojana” Mutual Fund for Public Investors
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company, as the promoter, and Nepal Life Capital Limited, as the plan manager, have launched the Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana, a collective investment mutual fund, on Magh 4, 2082 BS.
The fund has a total of 16 crore units worth Rs. 1.6 Arba, with 15% reserved for the promoter and manager, and the remaining 13.6 crore units available for public subscription at Rs. 10 per unit. Applicants can invest a minimum of 100 units and up to 1.6 crore units.
This first closed-end scheme under Nepal Life Mutual Fund has a 10-year maturity, with applications open until Magh 8, 2082 BS through approved banks, financial institutions, and the online platform “Mero Share.” The fund received strong ratings from ICRA Nepal: AA- for financial safety and AMC3 for management quality.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Approves Dividend and Emphasizes Digital Transformation in 29th AGM
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance successfully held its 29th Annual General Meeting (AGM) on Poush 19, 2082 BS, chaired by Chairman Govind Sanghai. The company’s financial statements, including the profit and loss account, cash flow, and auditor’s report for FY 2081/82, were reviewed and approved.
A total dividend of 21.05% of paid-up capital (Rs. 190,095,555), comprising 16.05% cash dividend and 5% bonus shares, was unanimously approved for shareholders. Auditors for FY 2082/83 were appointed.
The AGM emphasized structural reforms, good governance, technology integration, risk management, customer-centric strategies, and digital transformation to strengthen Nepal Life Insurance’s position in the life insurance sector and ensure sustainable growth.

Headline: Nepal Life Launches “Samriddhi Lagani Yojana” Mutual Fund
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Ltd., along with Nepal Life Capital Ltd. as the plan manager, is launching the “Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana” mutual fund. The Securities Board of Nepal has approved the issuance of 16 crore units at Rs. 10 per unit, totaling Rs. 1.6 billion.
This is the company’s first closed-end 10-year fund, rated AA- by ICRA Nepal for safety and AMC Quality 3 for management quality. Funds raised will be invested in registered securities, listed shares, bank deposits, money market instruments, government bonds, and other approved instruments. The units will soon be available for public subscription.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Company is Auctioning 2,00,000 Units Of Promoter Shares From Poush 16
Full Content:
The existing promoters of
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
are selling 2,00,000 units of promoter shares in an auction to the general public from 16th Poush to 23rd Poush, 2082.
The existing promoters, the general public, and institutions are all eligible to bid for the auction. Rs. 100 is the minimum bid rate for the auction. The minimum bid quantity for the shares is 1000 units. Although bidders can bid for the entirety of the issue, they are required to abide by Nepal Rastra Bank's rule to not exceed the specified quantity of shares per entity.
Muktinath Capital has been appointed as the auction manager.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Unveils Book Closure Date for its 21.05% Dividend; Calls AGM on Poush 19
Full Content:

has called its 26th AGM on 19th Poush, 2082. The meeting will be held in Hotel Vishuwa, Birgunj, Parsa, starting at 9:00 AM that day.
Among the other agendas, the AGM will endorse a 21.05% dividend for the fiscal year 2081/82. The 404th meeting of the board of directors held on Mangsir 24 has decided to distribute a 16.05% cash dividend (including tax) and 5% bonus shares. The existing paid-up capital of NLIC is Rs. 9.02 Arba.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Proposes 21.05% Dividend for FY 2081/82
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
has proposed a 21.05% dividend worth Rs. 1.90 Arba for the fiscal year 2081/82.
The 404th meeting of the board of directors held on Mangsir 24 has decided to distribute a 16.05% cash dividend (including tax) and 5% bonus shares. The existing paid-up capital of NLIC is Rs. 9.02 Arba.
The dividend is subject to approval from the Nepal Insurance Authority and the upcoming AGM.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Upgrades Three Narayani Branches to Enhance Customer Services
Full Content:
As part of its strategy to expand services and enhance customer experience, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC) has relocated three branches in the Narayani region, Tadi (Ratnanagar Tadi 2), Bharatpur (Bharatpur 3, Shahid Chowk, Narayanghat), and Chanauli (Bharatpur 18), to modernized facilities. The move aims to provide faster, more convenient, and higher-quality services to both existing and new policyholders.
The inauguration was attended by CEO Raj Kumar Aryal, Chief Marketing Officer Ganesh Chaulagai, Provincial Head Iswor Bikal Sapkota, branch managers, and staff. Company leaders emphasized that upgraded infrastructure, digital record systems, and customer-friendly layouts will significantly improve service efficiency and customer satisfaction. NLIC continues to prioritize service quality, transparency, and customer-centric initiatives across its 148 branches and sub-branches nationwide.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Contributes NPR 1.5 Crore to Reconstruction Fund
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC) has donated NPR 1.5 crore to the Physical Infrastructure Reconstruction Fund established by the Government of Nepal. The contribution was made to support the repair, economic recovery, and relief efforts following damage to public infrastructure during the recent protests on 23rd and 24th Baishakh.
The donation was formally handed over to Hon. Finance Minister Rameshwor Khanal by NLIC’s Chairman Govind Lal Sanghai, Director Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal, and CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli on 2082/09/15. Speaking at the ceremony, the Chairman emphasized the company’s commitment to corporate social responsibility and pledged continued support for government-led reconstruction and development initiatives. The Finance Minister thanked NLIC for its contribution, highlighting the importance of such support for Nepal’s infrastructure development.

Headline: Aayu Entertainments to Issue IPO for Fishtail Dream Park with 20% Public Offering
Full Content:
Aayu Entertainments Limited is set to issue an IPO for 20% of its paid-up capital at a face value of Rs. 100 per share to the public for its project, Fishtail Dream Park in Pokhara. The company has appointed Nepal Life Capital Limited as the issue and sales manager for the issuance of 30,00,000 shares. The agreement was signed by Chairman Kadam KC of Aayu Entertainments and CEO Manish Ghimire of Nepal Life Capital.
Fishtail Dream Park, developed with investment from the Sarathi Group and top entrepreneurs from Pokhara’s tourism sector, spans 57 ropani and is Nepal’s largest entertainment park, featuring a water park, rope bridge, and various adventure activities. Nepal Life Capital, a subsidiary of Nepal Life Insurance, is a licensed merchant banking institution authorized for investment management, underwriting, depository services, institutional advisory, share registration, and issue management.

Headline: Nepal Life Capital Limited's Mutual Fund Scheme "Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana" Worth Rs 1.60 Arba Added in SEBON Pipeline
Full Content:
The Securities Exchange Board of Nepal (SEBON) has recently added
"Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana"
under preliminary review in the latest list of mutual fund scheme pipeline status published.
Nepal Life Samriddhi Lagani Yojana is a closed-end mutual fund scheme that will have a fund size of Rs. 1.60 Arba divided into 16 Crore units, having a par value of Rs. 10 per unit. The application was sent to SEBON on Bhadra 15, 2082.
Nepal Life Capital Limited is the fund manager of the mutual fund scheme.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Becomes First Insurer to Receive Double A Minus Rating from ICRA Nepal
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited, Nepal’s most trusted life insurer, has received a prestigious Double A Minus (ICRA NP AA–) credit rating from ICRA Nepal, the highest in the country’s life insurance sector. This rating signifies very high safety and a strong capacity to meet financial obligations on time.
The recognition reflects Nepal Life’s robust financial stability, leading 27% market share, and 150.40% solvency ratio, well above the regulatory minimum. The company manages over 190 branches, maintains an investment portfolio exceeding NPR 240 billion, and has paid more than NPR 67 billion in claims. With 98.8% of its business in traditional life insurance and a disaster fund of NPR 1.32 billion, it demonstrates strong long-term stability.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli expressed gratitude to all stakeholders, emphasizing Nepal Life’s commitment to diversifying investments, strengthening financial resilience, and adhering to best national and international practices to ensure sustainable growth and trust.

Headline: ICRA Nepal Assigns AA- Credit Rating to Nepal Life Insurance for High Financial Safety
Full Content:
ICRA Nepal Limited has assigned an issuer rating of [ICRANP-IR] AA- to Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited, indicating a high degree of safety in meeting financial obligations and very low credit risk.
The rating reflects the company’s strong creditworthiness but is a general opinion, not tied to any specific debt instrument. The “AA-” rating falls one notch below “AA” and one above “A+” in the rating scale.

Full Content:
Insurance companies are competing with each other to increase their premium collection. Till the two months of the fiscal year 2082/83, i.e., Bhadra end, the life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 35.24 Arba, out of their 11,450,477 total active insurance policies.
As per the report published by Nepal Insurance Authority, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited limited single-handedly collected Rs. 9.68 Arba, having an active number of insurance policies of 1,642,239 as of Bhadra 2081.
Meanwhile, the most striking revelation comes from Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Co Ltd, which boasts the highest number of active insurance policies—2,436,828. However, the company generated only Rs. 1.01 Arba in premiums during the assessed period.
Coming towards the non-life insurance sector, Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Company collected the highest premium worth Rs. 89.44 Crores. Likewise, Shikhar Insurance Limited, which has 50,550 insurance policies, collected a premium worth Rs. 84.82 Crores as its insurance premium.
The non-life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 8.12 Arba out of its 432,114 total active insurance policies.

Headline: Project Care: Nepal Life Leads Everest Clean-Up to Tackle Mountaintop Pollution
Full Content:
Mount Everest is facing a growing pollution crisis, and Nepal Life Insurance Company, in partnership with Round Table Nepal, has launched “Project Care,” an Everest Clean-Up Campaign.
The first phase successfully collected 5,000 kg of waste, with plans to manage an additional 25,000 kg.
Biodegradable waste is disposed of responsibly at base camp, while non-biodegradable waste, including plastics, climbing gear, and oxygen cylinders, is transported to Kathmandu for recycling through Khaalisisi, promoting a circular economy.
Supported by the Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee (SPCC), the campaign exemplifies effective corporate social responsibility, collaborative environmental action, and innovative logistical solutions.
The initiative demonstrates that strategic partnerships can tackle even the most challenging environmental problems while preserving Nepal’s natural heritage for future generations.

Headline: Comparative Analysis of Life Insurance Companies in Q4 FY 2081/82: Profits, Capital, and Ratios Unveiled
Full Content:
The 13 life insurance companies have released their fourth-quarter financial statements for FY 2081/82, shedding light on their overall performance throughout the year. These reports provide insights into profitability, capital base, and the pace of business growth within the sector. It is worth noting that
Rastriya Jeewan Beema Company (RJBCL)
is among these insurers but is not listed on the stock exchange. This overview highlights key trends in earnings, capital adequacy, and other critical financial metrics shaping the industry’s outlook.
Net Profit:
In Q4 FY 2081/82, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC) led with a net profit of Rs. 60.33 Crores, marking a 17.37% increase over the same period last year. IME Life Insurance Company (ILI) followed with a net profit of Rs. 58.33 Crores, though this represents a 4.65% decrease from the previous year.
Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Limited (RNLI) recorded the highest growth, a staggering 47.26% rise, while Life Insurance Corporation Nepal Limited (LICN) saw the largest decline at 61.92%.
Paid-Up Capital:
Himalayan Life Insurance Limited (HLI) holds the highest paid-up capital at Rs. 9.14 Arba, followed by Nepal Life Insurance Company (NLIC) at Rs. 9.03 Arba, and Life Insurance Corporation Nepal (LICN) with Rs. 5.50 Arba. Rastriya Jeewan Beema Company (RJBCL) has the lowest paid-up capital at Rs. 18 Crores.
Reserve and Surplus:
The combined reserve and surplus of all life insurance companies totaled Rs. 20.59 Arba, with the industry average standing at Rs. 1.58 Arba. Life Insurance Corporation Nepal (LICN) led with Rs. 4.31 Arba, followed by Nepal Life Insurance (NLIC) at Rs. 3.32 Arba and Citizens Life Insurance (CLI) with Rs. 1.98 Arba.
Life Insurance Funds:
Collectively, life insurance companies gathered Rs. 7.82 Kharba in life insurance funds, with five companies surpassing this average.
Nepal Life Insurance Company (NLIC) led at Rs. 2.35 Kharba, followed by Life Insurance Corporation Nepal (LICN) at Rs. 1.33 Kharba. Sun Nepal Life Insurance (SNLI) recorded the lowest life insurance fund collection at Rs. 10.11 Arba.
Investments:
Nepal Life Insurance (NLIC) topped the list in investments with Rs. 1.89 Kharba, followed by Life Insurance Corporation Nepal Limited (LICN) with Rs. 1.17 Kharba.
Meanwhile, Sun Nepal Life Insurance (SNLI) had the smallest investment portfolio at Rs. 14.21 Arba.
Net Premium:
Net premium, reflecting the core company's earnings, saw Nepal Life Insurance (NLIC) leading at Rs. 47.67 Arba, closely followed by National Life Insurance Company (NLICL) at Rs. 21.47 Arba.
Income from Investments, Loans & Others:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC) has reported the highest income from investments, loans & others of Rs. 16.31 Arba. National Life Insurance Company Limited (NLICL) has reported a income from investments of Rs. 5.84 Arba, making it the second-highest.
Sun Nepal Life Insurance (SNLI) recorded the lowest earnings from investments, loans & others collection at Rs. 90 Crores.
Net Claims Paid:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC) holds the highest amount of net claim payment in this quarter, which amounts to Rs. 57.32 Arba. This is followed by Life Insurance Corporation Nepal Limited (LICN), which has a net claim payment of Rs. 26.84 Arba.
Total Inforce Policy Count:
Among the life insurance companies,
RNLI
is leading the chart with 24.94 lakh policies. Whereas,
PMLI
has the lowest total in-force policy count of 2.75 lakh.
Major Indicators:
Earnings Per Share (EPS):
Asian Life Insurance Company Limited (ALICL) posted the highest EPS at Rs. 12.04, followed by Rastriya Jeewan Beema Company (RJBCL) at Rs. 11.77 and IME Life Insurance Company (ILI) at Rs. 11.67.
The industry average EPS was Rs. 8.73, with five companies above this benchmark. Life Insurance Corporation Nepal Limited (LICN) had the lowest EPS at Rs. 5.74.
Net Worth Per Share:
Rastriya Jeewan Beema Company Limited (RJBCL) reported the highest net worth per share at Rs. 373.33, followed by Life Insurance Corporation Nepal Limited (LICN) at Rs. 187.47 and Sun Nepal Life Insurance (SNLI) at Rs. 154.35. Himalayan Life Insurance (HLI) recorded the lowest net worth per share at Rs. 111.2, while the industry average stood at Rs. 155.15.
P/E Ratio:
IME Life Insurance (ILI) had the lowest P/E ratio at 39.60 times, followed by Asian Life Insurance Company (ALICL) at 41.39 times. This reflects quarter-end ratios, and current ratios may vary with recent stock prices.
*Note: Rastriya Jeewan Beema Company (RJBCL) is not a listed entity; therefore, its P/E ratio is not applicable.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Concludes Grand Leadership Excellence Awards 2025, Honoring 440 Top Achievers
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company, Nepal’s most trusted life insurer, successfully concluded its three-day Leadership Excellence Awards 2025 at The Soaltee, Kathmandu, from Shrawan 16–18 under the theme "Lion Year: Lead, Roar, Repeat." The grand event saw the participation of 440 top-performing agents, agency managers, and company staff from across the country.
The program was inaugurated by board members Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal, Bimal Dhakal, and CEO Praveen Raman Parajuli. Leaders praised agents for achieving a historic milestone of NPR 10 billion in first-year premiums during FY 2081/82 despite economic challenges. The event included motivational speeches, strategic insights for FY 2082/83, and appreciation for contributions to the company’s growth.
A total of 440 high achievers were honored: 111 agency managers and 329 individual agents, with 96 awarded the Samrat Padak, 87 the Ratna Padak, and 257 the Samriddhi Padak. National-level winners also received cash awards. Motivational speaker and comedian Sandeep Chhetri delivered a special performance to conclude the event.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Bags Silver in NBPA-2024, Becomes First Life Insurer to Win Prestigious Reporting Award
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company, Nepal's most trusted life insurance provider, has been honored with the Silver Award in the National Best Presented Annual Report Award (NBPA-2024) by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nepal (ICAN). The award was conferred for the fiscal year 2080/81, recognizing the company’s excellence in financial reporting, transparency, accountability, and adherence to both national and international standards.
This makes Nepal Life the first life insurance company in Nepal to receive such recognition. The award was presented by Auditor General Toyam Raya to CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli and Deputy CEO Amit Kumar Keyal at an event in Hotel Radisson. CEO Parajuli expressed pride in the achievement and emphasized the company's continued commitment to financial transparency and good governance. He also extended gratitude to stakeholders, including board members, policyholders, agents, employees, shareholders, and regulatory bodies.

Headline: Nepal Life Achieves Historic Rs. 10 Arba First Premium Milestone
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC), Nepal’s most trusted life insurance provider, has achieved a historic milestone by earning Rs. 10 Arba in first premium income as it approaches its 25th anniversary.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli extended gratitude to the board, policyholders, agents, employees, shareholders, regulators, and all stakeholders for their support.
He emphasized that this achievement sets a benchmark in the insurance sector and reaffirms NLIC’s commitment to innovation, investment diversification, skill development, and delivering world-class insurance services using technology-driven solutions.

Headline: Nepal Life Contributes Rs. 10 Million to Boost Child Healthcare Infrastructure
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has provided Rs. 1 crore to the Kathmandu Institute of Child Health (KIOCH) under its corporate social responsibility (CSR) program to support the construction of a multi-specialty children's hospital in Budhanilkantha, Kathmandu. The agreement was signed by Dr. Bhagwan Koirala, KIOCH's founding chairperson, and Nepal Life CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli.
KIOCH’s hospital project is in its final phase, with a clinical research building already operational. During the signing event, both parties expressed their commitment to improving pediatric healthcare in Nepal. Nepal Life highlighted its ongoing CSR efforts and pledged future support for establishing similar hospitals across all provinces.
Dr. Koirala appreciated Nepal Life’s contribution, stating it would accelerate the project and strengthen their mission. KIOCH aims to function as a national resource center for pediatric healthcare, training, policy development, and quality standards. The organization has already launched its first operational hospital, KIOCH-Damak, which offers a full range of pediatric services, including emergency care, intensive care units, and modular operating theaters.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Powers Kathmandu Skills Fair 2082 to Empower Youth and Boost Employment
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has partnered as an institutional collaborator in the 'Kathmandu Metropolitan Skills Fair 2082' organized by Kathmandu Metropolitan City, showcasing its strong commitment to corporate social responsibility. The fair aims to provide free training in 37 professions across 10 fields, targeting unemployed youth, residents, taxpayers, and returnees from abroad.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli emphasized the importance of the fair in equipping youth with self-employment skills and bridging the gap between workforce supply and demand. Nepal Life sees the initiative not just as a training event, but as a transformative campaign for national prosperity and youth empowerment.
The fair, operating under the slogan "Employment and Income Growth, Prosperity of Kathmandu," is part of a three-year national pride project. It is conducted daily in three shifts and accommodates 25 trainees per session. Participants have expressed optimism about the future opportunities the training will bring.
Kathmandu Metropolitan representative Devendra KC praised the public-private collaboration, especially Nepal Life’s involvement. With over 3 million insured individuals, Nepal Life reaffirmed its ongoing commitment to providing quality services and supporting socially impactful initiatives like this skills fair.

Headline: Nepal Life Launches Investment Company to Diversify and Strengthen Capital Growth
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance has launched Nepal Life Investment Company Ltd. to enhance the management and diversification of its investment portfolio. The office was officially inaugurated by Govind Lal Sanghai, Chairman of Nepal Life, at Kamalpokhari. With an insurance fund of around Rs 250 billion, Nepal Life established this new company in response to provisions in the Insurance Act encouraging investment in specific and productive sectors like manufacturing.
The newly formed company's authorized capital stands at Rs 5 billion, with a paid-up capital of Rs 1.25 billion. CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli highlighted that the move aims not only at securing returns but also at capital protection, describing the initiative as a structural advancement for Nepal’s insurance sector. Chairman Sanghai emphasized the need to seek alternative investments due to falling savings interest rates. Subhash Thapa has been appointed as the CEO of the investment company.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Earns Rs. 65.2 Crores Net Profit in Q3; Net Worth per Share and EPS Decline
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
has posted a net profit of Rs. 65.2 crores in the third quarter of fiscal year 2081/82, reflecting an 8.64% growth compared to Rs. 60 crores in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Despite the profit increase, the company's annualized earnings per share (EPS) fell slightly to Rs. 9.63, down from Rs. 9.75.
The company’s paid-up capital reached Rs. 9.02 Arba, marking a 10% increase from the previous year’s Rs. 8.20 Arba. Similarly, its life insurance fund expanded by 15.41% to Rs. 22.70 Arba, indicating steady business growth. Investments rose to Rs. 18.45 Arba, up 12.45% from last year.
Net premium income rose by 11.61%, amounting to Rs. 32.50 Arba. Additionally, the company earned Rs. 12.12 Arba from investments, loans, and other income sources, which represents a 10.91% increase.
However, retained earnings declined sharply by 38.44%, falling to Rs. 11.83 crores from Rs. 19.23 crores. Net worth per share also dropped by 8.28% to Rs. 135.81, down from Rs. 148.07.
On the expenses side, net claim payments rose to Rs. 41.09 Arba, up by 13.83%. Commission expenses also increased by 10%, totaling Rs. 2.41 Arba this quarter.
Nepal Life Insurance is currently trading at a price-to-earnings (PE) ratio of 79.57.

Headline: Bonus Shares of Nepal Life Insurance Company and Aatmanirbhar Laghubitta Listed in NEPSE
Full Content:
82,07,966.55 unit bonus shares of
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
have been listed in NEPSE.
The company convened its 25th AGM on 28th Magh, 2081, and endorsed a 21.05% dividend from the profits of FY 80/81 for shareholders. The 388th meeting of the board of directors held on Poush 26 has decided to distribute an 11.05% cash dividend (including tax) and 10% bonus shares. The existing paid-up capital of NLIC is Rs. 8.20 Arba. The same bonus shares are now listed in NEPSE.
As of writing, NLIC has an LTP of Rs. 760.19.

Aatmanirbhar Laghubitta Bittiya Sanstha Limited (ANLB)
have been listed in NEPSE.
The company convened its 6th AGM on 29th Poush, 2081, and endorsed 14.25% bonus shares and 0.25% cash dividend (tax purposes) from the paid-up capital of Rs. 6.85 Crores, the bonus shares were worth Rs. 97.71 lakhs, and the cash dividend was worth Rs. 5.14 lakhs. The same bonus shares are now listed in NEPSE.
As of writing, ANLB has an LTP of Rs. 5,400.00.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Celebrates 24th Anniversary with Nationwide Blood Donation and Health Camp
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company (NLIC) marked its 24th anniversary with nationwide celebrations, including blood donation programs in 10 locations and a two-day free health camp at its Kathmandu office.
The company collected 412 pints of blood from various provinces, demonstrating its commitment to social responsibility. On this occasion, CEO Praveen Raman Parajuli expressed gratitude to all stakeholders and reaffirmed the company’s dedication to continued service and public trust.

Headline: Nepal Life Concludes Sales Transformation Session, Emphasizes Digitalization and Market Expansion
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company, Nepal’s most trusted life insurance provider, successfully held a one-day Sales Transformation Session in Kathmandu.
The event reviewed the third quarter performance of the current fiscal year and formulated sales strategies for the remaining period of FY 2081/82.
Attended by top executives, including Chairman Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal and CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli, the session emphasized the importance of teamwork, strategic implementation, and innovation in insurance.
The company aims to enhance insurance awareness, increase market reach, and fully digitize services to improve customer access. Officials stressed adapting to global trends and AI-driven transformations in the insurance sector.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Wins 'Best Life Insurance Company of The Year 2025' Award
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has been awarded the "Best Life Insurance Company of The Year 2025" at the 17th Corporate Business Awards 2025, organized by Corporate Khabar. The award recognizes Nepal Life for its excellence in financial management, good governance, high claim settlement ratio, human resource development, and advancements in automation and digital transformation.
The company’s transparency, effective operations, and trustworthiness contributed to its win. Amit Kumar Keyal, Deputy CEO of Nepal Life, received the award at a grand ceremony in Kathmandu. CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli expressed gratitude to the board members, staff, agents, regulators, shareholders, and valued customers for their collective efforts in achieving this success and promoting the importance of life insurance in Nepal.

Headline: Nepal Life Partners with Round Table Nepal for Everest Clean-Up Campaign
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance has signed an agreement with Round Table Nepal under Project Care to clean up Everest. The initiative, supported by the Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee, aims to collect 5,000 kg of waste this season and 25,000 kg in the future.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli emphasized Everest's global significance and the need for conservation. Representatives highlighted the increasing waste problem due to mountaineering activities and the importance of sustainable solutions. The campaign will transport non-biodegradable waste to Kathmandu while managing biodegradable waste at lower altitudes.

Headline: Life and Non-Life Insurance Sectors Report Varied Performance in Premium Collection Till Falgun FY 2081/82
Full Content:
Insurance companies are competing with each other to increase their premium collection. Till the eight months of the fiscal year 2081/82 i.e. Falgun end, the life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 1.08 Kharba, out of its 13,446,792 total active insurance policies.
As per the report published by Nepal Insurance Authority, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited limited single-handedly collected Rs. 29.39 Arba, having an active number of insurance policies of 1,904,096 as of Falgun 2081.
Meanwhile, the most striking revelation comes from Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Co Ltd, which boasts the highest number of active insurance policies—2,475,902. However, the company generated only Rs. 3.17 Arba in premiums during the assessed period.
Coming towards the nonlife insurance sector, Shikhar Insurance Company collected the highest premium worth Rs. 4.01 Arba. Likewise, Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Limited, which has 185,087 insurance policies, collected a premium worth Rs. 3.32 Arba as its insurance premium.
The non-life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 28.02 Arba out of its 1,843,456 total active insurance policies.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Unveils Calendar for 2082 BS
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance, Nepal’s most trusted life insurance company, has launched its 2082 BS calendar during a special event at its central office in Kamaladi on Chaitra 7, 2081. The calendar includes holidays, festivals, significant dates, and Panchang details.
The unveiling was done jointly by CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli, Deputy CEO Amit Kumar Keyal, Chief Business Operations Officer Om Prakash Pudasaini, and CFO Prem Prasad Regmi.
On this occasion, CEO Parajuli extended New Year 2082 best wishes to customers, agents, employees, stakeholders, and regulatory bodies. He emphasized the company’s commitment to innovation and service enhancement, promising to introduce technology-driven plans to meet customer expectations and strengthen Nepal Life’s position further.

Headline: Nepal Life Elects New Directors, Sworn In at Board Meeting
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited held its 25th Annual General Meeting, completing the postponed election of public shareholder directors.
Bimal Prasad Dhakal, Krishna Raj Lamichhane, and Sharmila Shrestha Maharjan were elected as directors.
Following the election, they were sworn in and assumed office in the 393rd board meeting on Chaitra 2, 2081, under the Insurance Act 2079.

Headline: Nepal Life Unveils “Chhutla Hai, Chhut” with 50% Renewal Fee Discount
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has introduced the "Chhutla Hai, Chhut" scheme, which offers a 50% discount on late renewal fees for policies that have been inactive for more than 180 days. Policyholders can renew their policies between 2081/11/15 and 2082/02/13 to avail of this offer.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli announced this scheme as the company enters its 25th year, urging policyholders to renew their policies on time for continued coverage and financial security.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Holds 25th AGM, Declares 21.05% Dividend and Announces Future Plans
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance held its 25th Annual General Meeting (AGM) on 28th Magh, 2081, at Hotel Vishuwa, Birgunj, chaired by the Board Chairman Govind Lal Sanghai.
During the meeting, the annual progress report for FY 2080/81 was discussed and approved, along with financial statements, including the balance sheet, profit and loss account, and cash flow.
The meeting also approved the appointment of auditors for FY 2081/82 and declared a 21.05% dividend, including 10% bonus shares and 11.05% cash dividend.
Chairman Sanghai expressed the company's commitment to advancing its business and services through structural reforms, improved governance, and the use of modern technology.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli highlighted the achievements despite economic challenges and announced plans for the company's 25th-anniversary celebrations in the upcoming year.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Company Q2 Report: Net Profit Surges 9.45%, Net Premiums Rise 12.26%, Investment Income at Rs. 9.22 Arba
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
has delivered a remarkable financial performance in the second quarter of fiscal year 2081/82, achieving a 9.45% increase in net profit. The company’s net profit rose to Rs. 46.81 Crores, up from Rs. 42.77 Crores in the same quarter of the previous year.
NLIC's financial base includes a paid-up capital of Rs. 8.2 Arba, with additional reserves comprising Rs. 2.38 Arba in retained earnings, Rs. 78.26 Crores in other equity, and Rs. 1.3 Arba in catastrophe reserves.
The quarter saw a 12.26 % growth in net premiums, totaling Rs. 22.12 Arba, alongside Rs. 9.22 Arba generated from investments, loans, and other financial activities. However, net claims surged by 15.94% to Rs. 28.54 Arba, and commission expenses rose by 9.82% to Rs. 1.63 Arba.
NLIC’s key financial indicators remain strong, with an annualized earnings per share (EPS) of Rs. 11.42, a net worth per share of Rs. 154.55, and a Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio of 70.47.

Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC).

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Company Holds Grand 'MDRT Achievers Award, 2025' Ceremony
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company celebrated the completion of its 'MDRT Achievers Award 2025' event on Magh 5, 2081, at The Soaltee Kathmandu, recognizing 95 agents who qualified for the MDRT 2025.
The event was inaugurated by company directors Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal, Shakti Kumar Golyan, and CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli.
CEO Parajuli highlighted Nepal Life's market leadership and the importance of agents in the company's success, emphasizing the potential of Nepal’s insurance market.
Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal praised the agents for their achievements, despite economic challenges, and urged them to gain international exposure.
Agents expressed gratitude for the company's support in skill development and their ongoing efforts to expand Nepal Life’s market share.
The program concluded with Deputy CEO Amit Kumar Keyal thanking the organizers and encouraging all MDRT qualifiers to aim for higher achievements in the future.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Unveils Book Closure Date for its 21.05% Dividend; Calls AGM on 28th Magh
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
has called its 25th AGM on 28th Magh, 2081. The meeting will be held in Hotel Vishuwa, Birgunj, Parsa, starting at 9:00 AM that day.
Among the other agendas, the AGM will endorse a 21.05% dividend for the fiscal year 2080/81. The 388th meeting of the board of directors held on Poush 26 has decided to distribute an 11.05% cash dividend (including tax) and 10% bonus shares. The existing paid-up capital of NLIC is Rs. 8.20 Arba.
Furthermore, an agenda is to endorse the auditor's report with PL statements, financial reports, and cash flow reports and appoint an auditor for the fiscal year 2081/82. There is an agenda to elect three directors from the public shareholding group.
The book closure date is on Magh 10. Therefore, the shareholders maintained before that day are entitled to dividend payout, and can attend this AGM.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Proposes 21.05% Dividend for FY 2080/81
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
has proposed a 21.05% dividend worth Rs. 1.72 Arba for the fiscal year 2080/81.
The 388th meeting of the board of directors held on Poush 26 has decided to distribute an 11.05% cash dividend (including tax) and 10% bonus shares. The existing paid-up capital of NLIC is Rs. 8.20 Arba.
The dividend is subject to approval from the Nepal Insurance Authority, and the upcoming AGM.
As of writing, NLIC closed at Rs. 782.00.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Introduces 'Rakshya Kavach Term Life Insurance Plan'
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance has launched the
'Nepal Life Rakshya Kavach Term Life Insurance Plan'
, offering maximum financial protection at minimal premiums. Unveiled by CEO Praveen Raman Parajuli on December 18, 2024, the plan provides coverage ranging from
Rs. 5 lakhs to Rs. 1 crore
for individuals aged 18 to 59, with policy terms from 1 to 35 years. In case of the insured’s demise during the term, the insured amount is paid, and the policy terminates. Optional riders like
ADB, ADB/PTD/PWB
are available for enhanced benefits.
The plan aims to ensure economic security for families, addressing today’s insurance needs. It can be availed either as a standalone policy or as an add-on to six existing plans, allowing significant risk coverage at an affordable cost. National Sales Head Umapati Pokharel emphasized its flexibility, while Deputy CEO Amit Kumar Kayal highlighted its focus on extending insurance accessibility across all income groups, enhancing Nepal Life’s portfolio and customer reach.
Training Department Head Rajesh Basnet provided a detailed presentation on the plan’s features and its integration with other savings and whole-life policies for added benefits. Nepal Life believes this initiative will cater to modern financial security needs, ensuring affordability and comprehensive protection while setting a new benchmark in Nepal's insurance sector.

Headline: Life and Non-Life Insurance Sectors Report Varied Performance in Premium Collection Till Mangsir FY 2081/82
Full Content:
Insurance companies are competing with each other to increase their premium collection. Till the four months of the fiscal year 2081/82 i.e. Mangsir end, the life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 65.74 Arba, out of its 13,342,246 total active insurance policies.

Coming towards the nonlife insurance sector, Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Limited collected the highest premium worth Rs. 2.19 Arba. Likewise, Siddhartha Premier Insurance Limited which has 125,155 insurance policies collected a premium worth Rs. 1.76 Arba as its insurance premium.
The non-life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 17.17 Arba, out of its 1,137,272 total active insurance policies.

Headline: Life and Non-Life Insurance Sectors Unveil Premium Collection Till Kartik FY 2081/82; NLIC and SALICO Lead Their Sectors
Full Content:
Insurance companies are competing with each other to increase their premium collection. Till the four months of the fiscal year 2081/82 i.e. Kartik end, the life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 53.39 Arba, out of its 13,349,157 total active insurance policies.
As per the report published by Nepal Insurance Authority, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited limited single-handedly collected Rs. 15.4 Arba, having an active number of insurance policies of 1,662,403 as of Kartik 2081.
Meanwhile, the most striking revelation comes from Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Co Ltd, which boasts the highest number of active insurance policies—2,514,187. However, the company generated only Rs. 1.55 Arba in premiums during the assessed period.
Coming towards the nonlife insurance sector, Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Limited collected the highest premium worth Rs. 1.77 Arba. Likewise, Siddhartha Premier Insurance Limited which has 99,424 insurance policies collected a premium worth Rs. 1.46 Arba as its insurance premium.
The non-life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 14.09 Arba, out of its 897,235 total active insurance policies.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Donates Rs. 1 Million to Samata Education Foundation
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited has donated Rs. 1 million to Samata Education Foundation as part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) efforts. The donation was presented by company director Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal and CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli.
Agrawal expressed gratitude towards the foundation for providing quality education to financially disadvantaged children, noting that this initiative will contribute significantly to nation-building.
CEO Parajuli emphasized that providing quality education to students will help develop skilled manpower for the country’s future.
Deepak Sanjel, President of Samata Education Foundation, shared that the foundation has been operating for 23 years and currently serves around 30,000 students across all 77 districts of Nepal. The foundation plans to build a renewable fund with the donation, ensuring long-term sustainability for its educational efforts.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Purchases Land and Building in Itahari for Office Use
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited has acquired land and buildings in Itahari, Sunsari District, with approval from the Nepal Insurance Authority. This property, located in Ward No. 6 of Itahari Sub-Metropolitan, is registered under the names Sandeep Gautam, Pratibha Khanal, and Ananta Singh.
Covering a total area of 91.50 dhur, the property includes plots numbered 476, 477, and 3158. The purchase, finalized on Kartik 28, 2081, was completed for a total cost of Rs. 16,79,56,889, which includes a registration fee of Rs. 72,32,594. This acquisition is intended for the business and office operations of Nepal Life Insurance Company.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Company Buys Land With Building in Hetauda
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited has bought land and a building in Hetauda. This purchase was approved by the Nepal Insurance Authority.
The property is located in Ward No. 4 of Hetauda, in the Makawanpur District. It is registered in the names of Dipendra Chand Thakuri and Surendra Chand Thakuri. The total area of the land is 60 dhur, which includes lot numbers 10467, 15887, 15888, 10469, and 10466. The total cost of the purchase is Rs. 17,89,51,500, including a registration fee of Rs. 79,51,500.

Headline: Life and Non-Life Insurance Sectors Report Varied Performance in Premium Collection Till Ashwin FY 2081/82
Full Content:
Insurance companies are competing with each other to increase their premium collection. Till the three months of the fiscal year 2081/82 i.e. Ashwin end, the life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 41.08 Arba, out of its 13,335,998 total active insurance policies.
As per the report published by Nepal Insurance Authority, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited limited single-handedly collected Rs. 11.99 Arba, having an active number of insurance policies of 1,644,219 as of Ashwin 2081.
Meanwhile, the most striking revelation comes from Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Co Ltd, which boasts the highest number of active insurance policies—2,514,187. However, the company generated only Rs. 1.2 Arba in premiums during the assessed period.
Coming towards the nonlife insurance sector, Sagarmatha Lumbini Insurance Limited collected the highest premium worth Rs. 1.43 Arba. Likewise, Siddhartha Premier Insurance Limited which has 74,789 insurance policies collected a premium worth Rs. 1.17 Arba as its insurance premium.
The non-life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs 11.38 Arba, out of its 668,140 total active insurance policies.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Launches New Learning Management System: "Nepal Life Pathshala"
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance launched its new "Nepal Life Pathshala," an online Learning Management System, in Kathmandu to enhance insurance training accessibility.
CEO Mr. Pravin Raman Parajuli inaugurated the platform, which offers agents remote audiovisual training aligned with the Insurance Board’s curriculum.
The platform is expected to expand training for company staff and improve insurance outreach across Nepal.
Additionally, a new QR code service was introduced for remote premium and loan payments, showcasing Nepal Life's commitment to digital innovation.
Senior leaders and industry representatives, including Mr. Umapati Pokharel and Mr. Tejmani Sharma Timilsina, praised the platform for modernizing training.
Mr. Amit Kumar Kayal, Deputy CEO, emphasized Nepal Life’s dedication to agility and innovation, underscoring the company’s efforts to adapt to technological advances as it marks 20 years in the industry.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Company Provides Relief to Flood Victims in Okhaldhunga
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has provided relief materials to flood victims in Okhaldhunga, Dhankuta, and Garjudhara as part of its corporate social responsibility efforts.
The company distributed essential items, including rice, lentils, salt, oil, and soap, to 45 families in Gauridanda, Jese, and Patle, with each family receiving 30 kg of rice, 2 kg each of lentils and salt, 2 liters of oil, and 4 soaps.
After severe rains from 9th to 12th Ashwin damaged three houses in Dhankuta, the company supplied zinc sheets and tents to affected households. Additionally, food assistance was provided to 30 families displaced by flooding in the Jhaple River.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli emphasized the company's commitment to socio-economic transformation and readiness to support affected families in the future.
The company is actively involved in various initiatives related to education, health, disaster relief, insurance awareness, and improving the lives of marginalized communities.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Launches TikTok Competition to Celebrate Bada Dashain
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company, recognized as the most reliable life insurance provider in Nepal, is hosting a TikTok competition to celebrate Bada Dashain and enhance enthusiasm among Nepalis.
Participants are encouraged to create original jingles, with cash prizes of Rs. 30,000, Rs. 20,000, and Rs. 10,000 awarded to the top three entries based on views, likes, shares, and submissions.
The competition runs from 17 Ashwin 2081 to 24 Kartik, inviting participants nationwide to showcase their creativity.
CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli urged everyone to join in and express their talents, assuring that similar events will be held in the future. He also extended best wishes for Bada Dashain 2081, Tihar, Nepal Sambat 1145, and the Chhath festival.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Releases Emotional Public Awareness Video to Promote Policy Retention
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company has released an emotional video to encourage policyholders to maintain their insurance policies and avoid surrendering them.
The video illustrates how a once-prosperous family can face financial hardship due to unforeseen accidents, emphasizing the importance of continuing insurance coverage.
It uses music to convey the emotional impact of losing insurance. Pravin Raman Parajuli, the CEO, highlighted that lack of awareness often leads to policy surrenders and urged people to keep their insurance for a secure future. The company plans to conduct more awareness programs to address this issue.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Posts 30.81% Profit Surge in Q4 FY 2080/81; Net Premiums and Investment Income Drive Growth
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
has reported a magnificent 30.81% increase in net profit for the fourth quarter of FY 2080/81, reaching Rs. 51.39 crore, up from Rs. 39.29 crore in the same quarter of the previous fiscal year.
NLIC maintains a strong financial position with a paid-up capital of Rs. 8.2 Arba. Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Company Concludes Grand Leadership Excellence Awards 2024
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company successfully concluded its three-day Leadership Excellence Awards 2024 at Tiger Palace Resort, Bhairahawa, attended by 191 agencies, agency managers, and company employees.
The event, held from the 11th to the 13th of Shrawan, celebrated outstanding performances under the theme "Hak Barsh Fly High, Aim Higher." The program was inaugurated by company director Bimal Dhakal and CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli.
Virtually addressing the gathering, Chairman Gobind Lal Sanghai and other executives congratulated and thanked the agents and employees for their exceptional performance in the fiscal year 2080/81 despite economic challenges. They highlighted the company's commitment to investment diversification and improving the standard of living for insurance agents.
CEO Parajuli emphasized the critical role of agents in the company's success and outlined the sales strategy for the current fiscal year. National Sales Head Umapati Pokharel praised the agents and staff for their contributions and stressed the importance of bringing insurance to the common people.
The event recognized top-performing agents with awards and medals, including the Samrat Medal, Ratna Medal, and Samriddhi Medal. The best agents were also honored with cash prizes, acknowledging their significant contributions to the company's growth.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Expands Portfolio with Strategic Investments in Education
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited, a leading life insurance provider in Nepal, has decided to diversify its investments by acquiring stakes in Professional Educators Limited and Uniglobe Higher Secondary School. On Shrawan 6, 2081, at Hotel Royal Singi in Kathmandu, the company signed agreements to invest Rs 73.72 crore for a 35.32% stake in Professional Educators Limited and Rs 60 crore for a 47.62% stake in Uniglobe Higher Secondary School.
Key Points:
1. Investment Details: Nepal Life Insurance will hold significant ownership in both entities, reflecting its strategy for investment diversification and focus on the education sector.
2. Company Statements: Chairman Mr. Govind Lal Sanghai stated that the investment aligns with regulatory guidelines and aims to contribute positively to the nation through the education sector. CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli emphasized the company's commitment to investment diversification and high returns.
3. Sector Impact: The investments are intended to enhance Nepal Life's portfolio and provide better returns while contributing to national development.
4. Collaboration: Professional Educators Limited's Executive Chairman Prof. Dr. Khagendra Prasad Ojha welcomed the partnership, viewing it as a milestone for both sectors.
The move underscores Nepal Life Insurance's strategic focus on enhancing its investment portfolio while supporting national development through education.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Holds 23rd and 24th Annual General Meetings in Birgunj
Full Content:
The 23rd and 24th Annual General Meeting of Nepal Life Insurance, chaired by Mr. Govind Lal Sanghai, was held at Hotel Vishuwa in Birgunj, Parsa. The meeting approved the annual work progress reports, financial statements, and auditor's reports for FY 2078/79 and FY 2079/80. The appointment of auditors and their remuneration for FY 2079/80 and FY 2080/81 were also approved.
A proposal for a cash dividend of 21.05% (including tax) worth Rs. 1,72,79,92,949/- from the distributable profits of 2079/80 was unanimously passed. Additionally, a proposal to amend the board's structure to include directors from both founding and general groups and an independent director was approved.
Chairman Sanghai committed to advancing the company through structural reforms, corporate governance, internal controls, technology adoption, and customer-centric strategies. He emphasized the company's adherence to international professional standards and plans for digital transformation and risk management.
Director Kamlesh Kumar Agrawal and CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli addressed shareholder suggestions and highlighted the company's achievements, including a market share increase to 26.06% in FY 2079/80. Despite economic challenges, Nepal Life Insurance maintained strong performance with Rs. 200.54 Arba in investments, Rs. 189.18 Arba in the life insurance fund, and Rs. 11.66 Arba in shareholders' funds. The company operates through 193 offices nationwide, has issued over 3.55 lakh policies, and remains committed to providing additional services and facilities as needed.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Steps Up with Relief Distribution in Matihani Municipality
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company (NLIC) recognized as a leading life insurance provider in Nepal, has stepped forward to aid families affected by a devastating fire in Matihani Municipality Ward No. 6, Mahottari. In a relief distribution event attended by local officials including the municipality chief Hari Prasad Mandal and Ward Chairman Kalim Rain, the company distributed a saree to each household impacted by the fire.
At the event, Mandal acknowledged and appreciated the company's timely support, emphasizing its importance in helping the families recover. Rain also highlighted how the assistance would ease the burdens of those families, particularly due to the loss of clothing and other essentials.
The CEO of Nepal Life Insurance, Pravin Raman Parajuli, reiterated the company’s commitment to societal well-being through various socio-economic activities under its corporate social responsibility (CSR) program. He assured ongoing support for the affected families and readiness to lead future assistance initiatives.
The company’s CSR efforts span education, health, disaster relief, insurance awareness, infrastructure, and support for the underprivileged. Overall, the company provided relief materials to 150 households, addressing the needs arising from the fire that destroyed over 100 houses and damaged around 50 in the ward.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Marks 23rd Anniversary with Free Health Camp
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC) celebrated its 23rd anniversary by hosting a free health camp over two days at its central office in Kathmandu. The event attracted over 500 attendees, including employees, agents, customers, and the general public.
A range of medical services such as ECGs, echocardiograms, lipid profiles, and blood pressure tests were provided, along with doctor consultations and free medications.
The CEO, Mr. Pravin Raman Parajuli, emphasized the importance of regular health check-ups and announced plans to extend these services to marginalized and economically disadvantaged communities in remote areas of Nepal.
This initiative is part of the company's Institutional Social Responsibility program and aims to strengthen ties with stakeholders and promote health awareness.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Launches Children's Golden Future Plan for Educational and Financial Security
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC) has launched a new life insurance policy called the Nepal Life Children's Golden Future Life Insurance Plan, aimed at ensuring financial security for children's education and future needs.
Unveiled by CEO Pravin Raman Parajuli during a ceremony in Kamaladi, this plan offers comprehensive coverage from a child's early age until maturity. The insurance is available for children aged 1 month to 17 years, with proposers aged 21 to 65 years eligible to apply.
The plan provides flexibility in premium payments, spanning 5 to 25 years, and includes features such as risk coverage starting at different points for the child and the proposer, and continuation of the policy without premiums if the proposer passes away.
The plan offers a lump-sum payment of the sum assured and bonuses at the end of the term, with provisions for payouts in cases of the child's or proposer's death during the term under specified conditions.
Policyholders can also avail themselves of loans against the surrender value of the policy and opt for additional benefits such as accidental death and critical illness coverage by paying extra premiums. The plan, supported by the Nepal Insurance Authority and other stakeholders, is designed to be flexible with various payment options and encourages widespread participation to secure children's futures.

Headline: Nepal Life Capital Promotes Financial Literacy through Global Money Week
Full Content:
Nepal Life Capital, in collaboration with Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC), organized a financial literacy program during "Global Money Week" from March 18 to March 24.
The program aimed to educate the public on investment strategies for a prosperous future. Interaction sessions were conducted at five different locations outside the valley, focusing on the securities market, investment, and risk reduction.
Participants received insights on investment methods, future benefits, and risks associated with investing from a young age. With 500 beneficiaries, the program emphasized the importance of understanding the impact of the stock market and its returns.
Nepal Life Capital, licensed for merchant banking by the Securities Board of Nepal, aims to mobilize savings through Nepal's capital market, offering investment management and Demat account services to provide safe and profitable investment opportunities for Nepali investors.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance Hosts Insightful Program on Industry Trends
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance, a leading life insurance company, organized a special interaction program in Kathmandu, featuring Philip Jackson from the Milliman Group, a renowned actuarial and consulting organization.

Headline: Nepal Life Insurance's Initiative Against Money Laundering And Terrorism Financing
Full Content:
Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited (NLIC)
, recognized as the most reliable life insurance company in the nation, recently conducted training on Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) for its board members and department heads, in adherence to Section 15 of Directive 2075 on Prevention of Financial Investments in Asset Laundering and Terrorist Activities.
The training, held at Soaltee Westend Resort in Dhulikhel, covered topics such as money laundering, terrorist activities, and potential challenges faced by financial institutions, alongside their solutions. Discussions also centered around Nepal's mutual evaluation report concerning the insurance sector, emphasizing strategies for compliance.
The program delved into the responsibilities and rights of the board of directors as per the Asset Clearance Act, focusing on effective implementation strategies. Nepal Life Insurance is determined to mitigate future incidents through insights gained from past crimes.
The company underscored the importance of adhering to international best practices and local regulations to combat money laundering effectively and safeguard the nation from criminal and terrorist activities.
Chairman Govind Lal Sanghai expressed the company's commitment to leading in this endeavor. Pravin Raman Parajuli stressed the importance of strict adherence to policies and regulations in reducing financial crimes, highlighting the significance of such training sessions in fostering awareness of legal provisions.

Headline: Government Records Rs. 12.5 Arba Profit Tax Collection from Mergers, Acquisitions, and FPOs as BFIs Meet Deadline
Full Content:
The Large Taxpayer Office revealed the collection of Rs. 12.5 Arba in profit tax from mergers, gains from acquisitions (bargain purchases), and profits derived from Follow-On Public Offerings (FPOs). This substantial amount was collected over the course of Friday and Saturday, with meticulous filings by numerous organizations.
On Friday, a total of 30 organizations contributed to this figure by filing taxes amounting to Rs. 11.3 Arba. The momentum continued on Saturday, with an additional 11 institutions filing taxes, totaling Rs. 1.44 Arba. Mr. Janak Sharma, the head of the Large Taxpayer Office, provided these details, emphasizing the proactive engagement of both public and private entities in fulfilling their tax obligations.
Crucially, it was revealed that among the 41 organizations that paid taxes on profits from FPO, 14 of them also paid taxes on profits from both FPO and bargain purchases resulting from mergers and acquisitions. The taxes collected fall under the purview of the current financial year, marking a significant boost in revenue generation.
The background of this revenue collection effort includes persistent recommendations from the Office of the Auditor General. Since the 57th annual report published in 2077 BS, concerns were raised regarding tax evasion related to premiums of FPO, gains from bargain purchases in mergers and acquisitions, and auction share sales. Despite the repeated concerns, the Ministry of Finance and the Inland Revenue Department initially overlooked the issue.
However, the 60th report of the Office reiterated the importance of recovering revenues from these sources. Finance Minister Dr. Prakash Sharan Mahat responded to these concerns by introducing an arrangement. According to this arrangement, companies paying taxes in premiums of FPO, bargain purchase gains of mergers and acquisitions, and auction share sales by the end of Mangsir would be exempted from fines and interests. The government intended to encourage timely payment of revenues.
This move faced legal scrutiny when 16 Banking and Financial Institutions (BFIs) filed a petition challenging the taxation initiative. The BFIs alleged that the government's decision to grant exemptions on fees and fines was unconstitutional, asserting that it amounted to imposing taxes against the constitutional framework. However, the constitutional bench of the Supreme Court recently dismissed the petition, upholding the government's position. The court ruled that the taxation did not constitute a levy on capital.
The formal announcement of the dismissal was made on last Thursday under the constitutional bench of Chief Justice Bishowambhar Prasad Shrestha, affirming the government's approach to taxation in this context.
BFIs were given a deadline to deposit the specified amount by the end of Mangsir, with the incentive that they would not be charged interest and penalties. As a result, companies proactively met this deadline, contributing significantly to the substantial revenue collection observed over the weekend.

Headline: Life Insurance Companies Take Strategic Measures To Fulfil Capital Requirements Set by Insurance Authority
Full Content:
In order to fulfil the capital requirements set by Nepal Insurance Authority (NIA), life insurance companies in Nepal have been diligently implementing various strategies. Previously, the regulatory body had urged these companies to raise their paid-up capital to Rs. 5 Arba by the end of Chaitra 2079.
However, the deadline to enhance paid-up capital was extended till Ashad's end due to numerous insurance companies' failures to maintain the minimum capital required by the board. To meet the specified capital requirement, insurance companies have adopted various strategies, including pursuing mergers.
Until last year, there were 19 life insurance companies. Out of that, 12 companies were listed in NEPSE, 4 companies was in the process to go public, whereas, 3 were reluctant to issue an IPO. After the NIA minimum capital requirement directives, companies were compelled to go for merger. Hence 9 companies have merged reducing to 4 companies, due to which the total number of listed companies has come down to eight. Whereas, 4 are in the final process to issue IPO to the general public and 2 are still reluctant to go public. However, despite these consolidation efforts, several companies are still facing capital deficits.

SuryaJyoti Life Insurance Company, Prabhu Mahalaxmi Life Insurance, and Sanima Reliance Life Insurance Company remain in a capital deficit of Rs. 46 Crores, Rs. 71 Crores, and Rs. 82 Crores, respectively. Additionally, Asian Life Insurance Company and Life Insurance Corporation Nepal (LICN) are also grappling with capital deficits of Rs. 1.85 Arba and Rs. 2.35 Arba, respectively. However, LICN has announced its intention to issue 88.45% rights shares to increase its capital.
IME Life Insurance Company, Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Company, Citizen Life Insurance Company, and Sun Nepal Life Insurance Company are all facing capital deficits even after the issuance of their initial public offerings (IPOs). IME Life Insurance Company and Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Company's capitals will only reach Rs. 4 Arba, resulting in a deficit of Rs. 1 Arba each. Similarly, Citizen Life Insurance Company's deficit will amount to Rs. 1.25 Arba, as its capital will only reach Rs. 3.75 Arba. Sun Nepal Life Insurance Company will face a deficit of Rs. 1.8 Arba, with its capital reaching only Rs. 3.2 Arba. Despite the equity gap, these companies may consider issuing bonus shares and right shares using the premium amount obtained from the IPOs.
Mr. Raju Raman Paudel, the spokesperson of the Nepal Insurance Association (NIA), excerpts that to bridge these capital shortfalls, companies will be issuing the right shares or bonus shares based on their fiscal year-end balance sheets. This strategic move aims to meet the prescribed paid-up capital of Rs. 5 Arba by the end of Ashad, as mandated by the Insurance Board.

Headline: Deadline for Life and Non-Life Insurance Companies To Raise Capital To Rs 5 Arba & Rs 2.5 Arba Extended Till Ashad 2080
Full Content:
The rule stating that life insurance companies must have a minimum paid-up capital of Rs. 5 Arba was directed by the Nepal Insurance Authority on the 10th of Chaitra 2078. Non-life insurance companies were also urged by the Insurance Board to raise their paid-up capital to Rs. 2.5 Arba by the end of Chaitra 2079.
However, the authority's decision of refusing to give insurance companies time to raise capital has now changed. The authority that had adopted the decision of not extending the period allowed for insurance companies to boost their capital withdrew from the decision at the last minute, when the deadline to increase the capital had passed.
The deadline to enhance paid-up capital, according to the authority, has been extended as a result of numerous insurance companies' failures to maintain the minimum capital required by the board. The authority has now decided to give insurance companies an additional three months to raise capital. By the end of Ashad, both life and non-life insurance companies must have the required minimum paid-up capital.
The Fiscal Act 2078/79 also exempts the insurance firm from paying capital gains tax, dividend tax, and employee retirement tax if the preliminary merger agreement is completed by the end of the fiscal year. In order to take advantage of this, many insurance companies executed a merger agreement before the deadline of the facility.
Life-Insurance Companies
In the fiscal year 2078/2079 and 2079/2080, nine of the nineteen life insurance companies made the decision to merge in order to raise their paid–up capital, reducing the total number of life insurance companies to fourteen.

NON-LIFE

Companies have been unable to raise the required minimum capital, despite going through the merger procedure. So in a conversation with Raju Raman Paudel, the Insurance Authority's spokesperson (executive director) regarding the capital requirement has asserted that the deadline to increase the paid-up capital had been extended by three months, i.e until Ashad 2080.
Additionally, when discussing companies that pursued the merger/acquisition route but were unable to increase the minimum capital necessary by the board, Paudel emphasized that those companies will be given the chance to enhance their capital by issuing the right shares. However, these right shares are dependent on the companies’ audited fourth quarter reports, and the right shares will be issued based on the profits the company has made up to the fourth quarter of FY 2079/80 i.e by Ashad end 2080.

Headline: PM Prachanda Directs to Halt Tax on Further Public Offering (FPO)
Full Content:
Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' has directed the stakeholders to postpone the decision on imposing a tax on share premium amount sold through the further public offering (FPO). The PM has also asked to seek a long-term solution to this issue.
The PM issued the such directive after the Confederation of Nepalis Industries (CNI) and Nepal Bankers' Association drew the PM's attention regarding the impacts of the taxation on the share's premium amount.
During the meeting with the business leaders, PM Prachanda vowed to advance the process to address this issue for the long term.
The banks and financial institutions (BFIs) had increased their paid-up capital through the FPO as per the directive of the central bank.
During that period, there was no taxation on FPO but the 58th annual report of the Office of the Auditor General mentioned that the FPO share's premium amount should come under the ambit of tax while concluding that the tax amount should be paid from such companies.

Headline: Life Insurance Companies Collect an Impressive Premium of Rs. 71.65 Arba Till Six Months of FY 79/80
Full Content:
Insurance companies are competing with each other to increase their premium collection. Through the six months of the fiscal year 2079/80, the life insurance companies collected a total premium of Rs. 71.65 Arba, out of its 14,109,150 total active insurance policies.
As per the report published by Nepal Insurance Authority, Nepal Life Insurance Company Limited single-handedly collected Rs. 18.63 Arba, having an active number of insurance policies of 940,249 as of Poush, 2079.
Similarly, Mahalaxmi Life Insurance Limited generated the least amount of premium i.e Rs. 75 crores, owing to its 35,492 active insurance policies.
Note: Surya Life Insurance Company Limited (SLICL)
and
Jyoti Life Insurance Company Limited (JLI)
received the final approval for the merger from the Insurance Authority on Mangsir 2 and from the Securities Board on Mangsir 25 and the life insurance companies conducted their integrated business from, Poush 7, 2079. The companies merged in the name of
Suryajyoti Life Insurance Company Limited (
SJLIC)
.
Likewise, the premium collected by SJLIC is calculated only after their joint integrated transaction, i.e 7 Poush, 2079.
On the other hand, the highest number of active insurance policies lies with Reliable Nepal Life Insurance Co Ltd, having subscribers of 3,676,041 as of Poush 79/80. Despite the enormous number, it was able to generate only Rs. 1.78 Arba as its premium amount.
Note:- Investors of all life insurance companies should understand the quality of insurance policies is important rather than number of insurance policies. Moreover, these policies might include scheme such as foreign employment insurance policy which provides less net premium so some insurance companies do not prefer such policies. Hence, judging an insurance company based only on number of insurance policies would be absurd.
